body:
B-128 (helper-b128), what is in and what is not.

IN (PR #63, built, not walked): the grey row on the library's own rows. (1) Server: POST refs/unavailable takes {"ids": [...]} as well as {"songs": [...]} (exactly one; merged ids answer for the survivor; a song with a file and an unknown id are null; no ref is made); info.features lists unavailable-ids, so an app never sends ids to an N-13 server that would answer 400 (docs/17: never try a route to find out); the app also reads 400/404/405 as "no verdicts". (2) App: a library row with no file that is not downloaded is asked about by ref id and marked under it (libraryMarkProvider: a song with a file, a downloaded song, a plain server's row and any row while the server is away are never marked). Search greys the row and the Top result (quiet circle, "..." stays). (3) A marked library row never tries: playLibraryTracks is the one place Search plays library rows from; the "..." menu (Play next, Add to queue, Download) and the swipe say the sentence. (4) A refusal for good (the player's songRefusal answer is song_unavailable, or start() finds the ref marked) bumps songRefusalsProvider: the 10-minute trust in "no problem" ends at once, visible lists ask again, a stale answer is dropped. The regression test is the owner's scenario end to end, seen failing without the fix.

DECISIONS (yours to overrule): (a) the phone does NOT copy the server's 7-day window: the 404 body is unchanged (reason, not window); re-asking gives reason, sentence and window from one source and gives an older server no mark it never made. If the re-ask fails the row stays playable-looking and the next tap is refused from memory with no YouTube look-up. (b) (d) of the brief, the merge: unchanged on purpose; the library row is a ref, the exact identity; making SongHit carry both ids adds a weaker key. (c) a permanent refusal goes straight to grey (the N-13 design note's recommendation). (d) ids on the same route, not a verdict on the feeds' refs (needs the files feed to carry refs with no file: the 300-rows-per-import objection).

NOT IN: PR #64 (stacked on #63: base is its branch; retarget to main after #63 merges) wires the playlist (S-17) and Liked Songs (S-15) rows now that #59 is merged: one question per stretch of 100 rows that is built, Play/Shuffle leave a marked song out. The split from one PR to two is deliberate: P1-17's second PR waits only for what #63 changes in playback_providers.dart and song_marks.dart, and #64 touches only detail_screens.dart. Queue (S-33) and Recently played (S-23) are not drawn and not marked; the "..." menu reads marks wherever it is opened (S-34 is drawn). Album/artist pages of the library hold only songs with files: nothing to mark.

TRAPS / FINDINGS: (1) the local row a tap leaves behind (a ref with no file that nothing of the person's points at) is never retired: dropUnused is called only with ids a feed page carries (B-126's family: junk rows); not fixed. (2) A test that taps through a real InstantPlayService needs a session; the refusal is simulated by songRefusalsProvider.refused(), and the wiring (askSongRefusal, InstantController) is tested on its own. (3) song_marks.dart: serverAwayProvider is read in songMarkProvider/check/songMarksCheckProvider only (P1-17 replaces the provider, the names awayCauseProvider/AwayCause are untouched). (4) playback_providers.dart: only the songRefusal closure and one import changed (askSongRefusal lives in song_refusals.dart).

Proved: server 4 tests, app library_marks_test 12, song_marks_test +12, encore_unavailable_test +6, song_refusal_marks_test 3, instant_play_test +2, playlist_marks_test 10 (#64); full app suite 2,817 and the whole server suite green locally. Not proved: anything on a phone or a real server; no outside request was made.
